## Where I stand
The Fernhill SAML ACS endpoint now verifies the assertion signature with signxml and checks conditions, audience and subject confirmation itself, plus replay protection in Redis. python3-saml/xmlsec was abandoned after the Alpine libxml2 mismatch; after fixes for ruff, mypy and the skew tests, CI came back green and PR #412 is merged into main. What is left is the staging metadata exchange for Thursday's demo and the follow-up SSO enforcement ticket.

- [en-cours] Fernhill's staging IdP metadata is not loaded and our staging SP metadata has not been sent yet.
- [prochaine-étape] Load their staging IdP metadata and send them ours by Wednesday EOD, for the demo Thursday 10:00 New York.
- [prochaine-étape] Create the separate ticket for enforcing SSO / disabling password login for Fernhill users.
- [essai-raté] python3-saml on Alpine: lxml and xmlsec loaded mismatched libxml2, and building lxml from source failed too (no crypto module), so it was replaced by signxml.
- [décision] Go with signxml, drop python3-saml and xmlsec entirely, write the condition checks with tests, and read attributes only from the verified signed_xml (source: t08)
- [décision] 120 s clock skew per the Fernhill contract annex; password login left untouched as a separate ticket (source: t12)
- [décision] No --admin and no --auto on the PR; Maya to be pinged directly (source: t21)
